read_mode: Full source audio processed locally; complete transcript read. Visual reading used timestamped sampled frames, dense sampling at UDC, selfie and film-removal passages. Not a claim of continuous frame-by-frame viewing.
method: ffprobe + FFmpeg extraction; Pillow contact sheets; direct image inspection. Published images matched pixel-exactly to PyAV-decoded frames to identify actual PTS (requested integer + 0.021 s). Native video is 720×360 at nominal 30 fps.

findings.finding: Host calls this the technology aesthetics live stream and explicitly says 2022; Axon 40 Ultra is identified verbally and on packaging.
Screen-on/off and colored-background demonstrations; host attributes visible ring to factory film; microscope introduced around 379 s.
Front-camera screen display micro-adjustment page; regional luminance/color adjustment. This shows display controls, not sensor exposure or measured transmittance.
Microscope imaging of display and UDC region; 560 s inserted micrograph labels screen vs camera region; blue emitting subpixels have visibly different shapes.
One host demonstrates face unlock with progressively covered face and then mask; no trials or error-rate statistics.
Actual front-camera selfie shown, enlarged on phone, then portrait and hairline crop inserted at 765 s. Original photo/exposure/beauty setting not supplied.
Host peels the factory film, shows screen after removal, requests future detailed tests, then jokes about reapplying the film.

limitations: Automatic speech has name/model/technical-word errors; claim-critical passages checked against subtitles and visible UI.
No light-meter, transmission spectrum, PSF/MTF, RAW, same-scene conventional selfie reference, or controlled video-call test for this handset.
